Top-level structure I recommend in the MAP GDoc:

- Stakeholder roster and RACI (who signs off on soft vs final acceptance)
- Milestones (week-by-week cadence)
- Eval plan (sample prompts, datasets, perf metrics, tolerance levels)

Suggested 30-day cadence (example):
- Week 0: Kickoff + infra handshake (expect infra contact from Marco)
- Week 1: Baseline perf runs and prompt set validation
- Week 2: Optimization (batching, cache, quant profiles)
- Week 3: Acceptance rehearsals with your sample traffic
- Week 4: Soft acceptance & knowledge transfer; final acceptance at end of week 5 if needed

Jonas and Marissa are on copy to help define acceptance criteria and the ops checklist. I left placeholder fields in the GDoc for your team to fill stakeholder names and preferred dates.

Thanks Ellen — looping in a few clarifying questions so the MAP acceptance section is actionable.

Questions for BlueArc (propose we add these as checkboxes in the GDoc):
- Sample traffic: can you provide a 24-hour traffic trace or representative prompt set? (anonymized is fine)
- SLO targets: you mentioned p95 latency earlier — can you firm up numeric targets (ms) and max acceptable error rate?
- Data residency: will the evaluation use any customer PII or internal corp data? If yes, we need an aligned NDA addendum and a short data handling checklist.
- Integration surface: will you use REST API only, or do you need a dedicated VPC/Dedicated instance during the pilot?

Acceptance criteria I propose we include in the MAP (short form):
- Performance: p95 < 350ms for payloads up to 1k tokens on our tuned quantized profile
- Reliability: <0.5% error rate over 72-hour window at agreed throughput
- Quality: top-3 candidate pass rate on your test prompts >= 85% (example metric, we should pick your rubric)

I added a short checklist in the GDoc for data and infra owners. Happy to run a pre-kickoff technical readout.

— Jonas
